ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r3.claim: Yamīn means a hand, whether right or left, as classical Arabic usage shows.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r3.anchor: “ a hand” irrespective of being right or left.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r4.claim: Moses’ question about the staff is affectionate, not a request for information, like a question to a child whose answer is already known.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r5.claim: The affectionate question concerns an object that will become the source of Moses’ miracles.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p21/r5.anchor: source of miracles at the hands of Moses (sws).

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r5.claim: God’s question about the staff draws Moses’ attention to the miracle: God already knows what it is, but will transform dry wood into a moving serpent and display His power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r5.anchor: وقد علم تعالى في الأزل ما هي وإنما سأله ليريه عظم ما يخترعه عز وجل في الخشبة اليابسة من قلبها حية نضناضة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r6.claim: Grammatically, ما is the subject, تلك its predicate, and بيمينك a circumstantial phrase governed by the demonstrative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r6.anchor: وما استفهام مبتدأ وتلك خبره وبيمينك في موضع الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows تلك to function as a relative pronoun meaning that which is in your right hand; Ibn ʿAṭiyya mentions this alone, but the author says this is a Kufan, not Basran, analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p320/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون تلك اسما موصولا

SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r1.claim: ما is an interrogative subject, تلك its predicate, and بيمينك is a circumstantial phrase governed by the meaning of pointing, as in 11:72.
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r1.anchor: " ما " مبتدأة استفهامية. و " تلك " خبره. و " بيمنيك " متعلق بمحذوف لأنه حال كقوله: وهذا بعلي شيخا

SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r2.speaker: الزمخشري، ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari makes تلك a relative pronoun meaning “that which”; Ibn Atiyya gives only this analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r2.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن تكون " تلك " موصولة بمعنى التي، و " بيمينك " صلتها. ولم يذكر ابن عطية غيره

SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r3.speaker: البصريون
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r3.claim: Basran grammarians do not treat demonstratives as relatives except ذا under stated conditions.
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r3.anchor: وهذا ليس مذهب البصريين، لأنهم لم يجعلوا من أسماء الإشارة موصولا إلا " ذا " بشروط

SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r4.claim: Kufans allow all demonstratives as relatives and construe the phrase as “what is in your right hand.”
SAMIN-DURR:20:17/r4.anchor: وأما الكوفيون فيجيزون ذلك في جميعها

ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r1.claim: تلك is an indefinite demonstrative-like noun that behaves like التي and can be followed by a relative clause; the sense is, What is that which is in your right hand?
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r1.anchor: تلك اسم مبهم يجري مجرى التي، ويوصل كما توصل التي، المعنى ما التي بيمينك

ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r2.claim: The apparent question elicits Moses' admission, establishing proof against him so he cannot deny it later; Zajjaj illustrates this with dyed water.
ZAJJAJ:v3p353#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الكلام لفظه لفظ الاستفهام ومجراه في الكلام مجرى ما يسأل عنه، ويجيب

ASAD-NOTES:20:16/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:16/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:16/r2.claim: God asks Moses what he is holding in his right hand.
ASAD-NOTES:20:16/r2.anchor: Now, what is this in thy right hand, O Moses?

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r1.claim: The narrative turns from what Moses was commanded for himself to the task involving creation and others.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r1.anchor: شروع في حكاية ما كلفه عليه السلام من الامور المتعلق بالخلق اثر حكاية ما أمر به من الشؤن الخاصة بنفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r2.claim: Ma is interrogative and may be the subject with tilka as predicate, or vice versa; making ma the predicate better fits the meaning and answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r2.anchor: خبره أو بالعكس وهو ادخل بحسب المعنى واوافق بالجواب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r3.claim: Bi-yaminika is attached to an omitted circumstantial predicate, meaning the staff settled in or held by the right hand; the demonstrative's meaning governs it.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r3.anchor: أي وما تلك قارة أو ماخوذة بيمينك والعامل فيه ما فيه من معنى الاشارة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats tilka as a relative pronoun, with bi-yaminika belonging to an omitted relative clause; this follows the Kufan view that demonstratives can all be relative, unlike the Basran restriction.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : تلك اسم موصول و ( بيمينك ) متعلق بمحذوف صلته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r5.claim: The question is confirmatory; Alusi postpones the explanation of its purpose to the following discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p174#2/r5.anchor: والاستفهام تقريرى وسياتى قريبا إن شاء الله تعالى بيان المراد منه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r8.speaker: أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r8.claim: Ahmad transmits that after God called Moses near, he clutched the staff and struggled upright while trembling, speechless and terrified, then crept to the tree before God asked what he held.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r8.anchor: وقد روى الامام أحمد أنه عليه السلام بعد أن ناده ربه سبحانه وتحقق أنه جل وعلا هو المنادى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r9.claim: Alusi suggests Moses may have mentioned leaning first because it best fit God's question about what was in his right hand.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p175/r9.anchor: وقيل : لعل تقديم التوكؤ عليها لأنه الاوفق للسؤال بما تلك بيمينك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r1.claim: God asks about the object in Moses' hand to comfort him: after being awed by divine speech, he can answer an easy question correctly and recover his composure.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r1.anchor: ايناس منه تعالى له عليه السلام فانه عليه السلام دهش لما تكلم سبحانه معه بما يتعلق بالالوهية فسأله عن شئ بيده

ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r2.claim: A reported analogy says that after death the believer is similarly asked about the faith held in worldly life; recalling it removes the awe of arriving in God's presence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r2.anchor: قيل وكذلك يعامل المؤمن بعد موته وذلك أنه إذا مات وصل إلى حضرة ذى الجلال فيعتريه ما يعتريه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r3.claim: Another explanation says God first showed Moses perfect divinity, then human limitation: asking about the staff's uses showed how even a present object exceeds what reason can know without divine guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p210/r3.anchor: لما عرفه كمال الالوهية اراد أن يعرفه نقصان البشرية فسأله عن منافع العصا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r2.claim: The confirmatory question focuses Moses on the staff so its transformation will be recognized as a miracle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r2.anchor: {وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى} سؤال تقرير، والحكمة في هذا السؤال: تنبيهه وتوقيفه على أنها عصا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r3.claim: As Arabs do, one asks about what is already known to elicit verbal acknowledgment as well as knowledge in the heart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p268#2/r3.anchor: وهذا على عادة العرب، يقول الرجل لغيره: هل تعرف هذا؟ وهو لا يشك أنه يعرفه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r1.claim: The question awakens Moses’ attention to the wonders God will show through the staff.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r1.anchor: { وما تلك } استفهام يتضمن استيقاظا لما يريه فيها من العجائب.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r2.claim: Bi-yamīnika may be circumstantial to the demonstrative’s meaning or attached to tilka.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r2.anchor: { بيمينك } حال من معنى الإشارة، وقيل صلة { تلك }.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r3.claim: Repeating Moses’ name increases familiarity and draws attention.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r3.anchor: { يا موسى } تكرير لزيادة الاستئناس والتنبيه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r9.claim: Moses understood the question as inviting the staff’s identity and ordinary uses, so he stated its nature and benefits before its transformation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:17-19/r9.anchor: وكأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم فهم أن المقصود من السؤال أن يذكر حقيقتها وما يرى من منافعها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r6.claim: Though God knows the answer, He gently asks about the exalted object in Moses' right hand to reassure him and establish a sign of the Hour through the swift transformation of his known staff.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r6.anchor: مريدا - بعد تأنيسه بسؤاله عما هو أعلم به منه - إقامة البينة لديه بما يكون دليلا على الساعة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r7.claim: Moses is invited to look closely at his familiar staff as it becomes a living creature, strengthening conviction and confirming those to whom he will be sent.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r7.anchor: بقلب العصا حية بعد تحقق أنها عصاه يقرب النظر إليها عند السؤال عنها ليزداد بذلك ثباتا ويثبت من يرسل إليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r8.claim: Moses answers that it is his staff, outwardly and inwardly.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r8.anchor: أي ظاهرا وباطنا { عصاي } ثم وصل به مستأنسا بلذيذ المخاطبة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r9.claim: He says he leans on and relies on it when tired or needing help over slips, descents, climbs, leaps, darkness and similar situations.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r9.anchor: أي أعتمد وأرتفق وأتمكن { عليها } أي إذا أعييت أو أعرض لي ما يحوجني إلى ذلك من زلق أو هبوط أو صعود

BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r10.claim: After listing how the staff serves his own needs, Moses turns next to the needs of his flock.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p15/r10.anchor: ثم ثنى بعد مصلحة نفسه بأمر رعيته فقال

DURR-FULL:v5p554/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r1.claim: Wahb’s account continues: Moses sees the tree’s light rise as a blazing column, hears God call, approaches trembling, and is told that the speaker is God Himself, nearer than his own self.
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r1.anchor: فلما رأى ذلك موسى قال: إن لهذه شأنا ثم وضع أمرها على أنها مأمورة أو مصنوعة

DURR-FULL:v5p554/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r2.claim: In Wahb’s report God asks about Moses’ staff although He knows its identity; Moses says he leans on it, beats leaves for his sheep, and has other uses for it.
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r2.anchor: فقال له الرب تبارك وتعالى: {وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى} قال: هي عصاي قال: ما تصنع بها

DURR-FULL:v5p554/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r3.claim: Wahb details the staff’s practical uses: its fork and crook handle branches, carry gear, make a shaded shelter, reach distant water, and defend the sheep from predators.
DURR-FULL:v5p554/r3.anchor: وكان لموسى في العصا مآرب كان لها شعبتان ومحجن تحت الشعبتين فإذا طال الغصن حناه بالمحجن

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r1.claim: The question asks the essence of the named thing, its reality by which it is what it is, as when one asks what Zayd is and answers that he is a human being.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r1.anchor: السؤال بما تلك عن ماهية المسمى أي : حقيقته

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r2.claim: Kāshifī places the address after Moses removed his sandals in the sacred valley.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (ون موسى نعلين بيرون كرد در وادي مقدس

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r3.claim: Mā is an interrogative predicate of tilka, which points to the staff; this parsing fits Moses’ answer better than reversing the construction.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r3.anchor: فما استفهامية في حيز الرفع بالخبرية لتلك المشار إليها أي : العصا

BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r4.claim: The specification of the right hand avoids possible confusion if Moses held a ring or another object in his left hand; a generic reference to his hand might have left him unsure what was asked.
BURSEVI:v5p286#3/r4.anchor: ولم يقل بيدك لاحتمال أن يكون في يساره شيء مثل الخاتم ونحوه فلو أجمل إليه لتحير في الجواب

BURSEVI:v5p287/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p287/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p287/r7.claim: Although God knows all, He asks so observers first identify an insignificant staff, then witness the extraordinary miracles made from it, like a goldsmith displaying an iron blank before turning it into armor.
BURSEVI:v5p287/r7.anchor: قلنا فائدته أن من أراد أن يظهر من الحقير شيئا نفيسا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r4.claim: God's question prompts Moses to attend and prepare to receive what follows, although God eternally knew what the object was.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r4.anchor: تقرير مضمنه التنبيه وجمع النفس لتلقي ما يورد عليها وإلا فقد علم الله ما هي في الأزل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r5.claim: In “in your right hand,” the phrase attaches to “that”; Ibn Atiyya compares the construction with a line by Yazid ibn Rabi'a.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p40/r5.anchor: وقوله بيمينك من صلة تلك وهذا نظير قول الشاعر يزيد بن ربيعة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says tilka is an indefinite demonstrative functioning like allati, so the question means ‘what is that which is in your right hand?’
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#2/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج تلك اسم مبهم يجري مجرى التي والمعنى ما التي بيمينك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the question prompts Moses to identify the staff himself, fixing his admission as proof before God makes it turn into a serpent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r6.anchor: ليجيب المخاطب بالإقرار به فتثبت عليه الحجة باعترافه فلا يمكنه الجحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r7.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r7.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says God saw Moses' awe and asked the question to reassure him and relieve his fear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p277#3/r7.anchor: أنه لما أطلع الله تعالى على ما في قلب موسى من الهيبة والإجلال حين التكليم أراد أن يؤانسه ويخفف عنه ثقل ما كان فيه من الخوف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r1.claim: The staff transformation is a manifest miracle and break with ordinary nature, proving that only God can do it and that it comes through a sent prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r1.anchor: هذا برهان من الله تعالى لموسى، عليه السلام، ومعجزة عظيمة، وخرق للعادة باهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r2.claim: Some commentators say God asked about the staff to put Moses at ease.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r2.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: إنما قال له ذلك على سبيل الإيناس له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r3.claim: Others take the question as confirmation: God points out that it is the familiar staff in Moses' hand before showing what He will do with it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p278#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال له ذلك على وجه التقرير، أي: أما هذه التي في يمينك عصاك

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r1.claim: The question is a prompt rather than a request for information: it focuses Moses' attention so he will recognize that something important is coming.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r1.anchor: إنه ليس هو استفهاما، وإنما هو تقرير؛ ليحضر ذهنه، ويعلم أنه لا يسأله إلا لأمر عظيم.

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r2.claim: Another explanation says God addressed Moses in ordinary human fashion when he was confused, to calm him.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r2.anchor: وقيل: لما تحير خاطبه بخطاب يجري بين الآدميين ليسكن قلبه.

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r3.claim: A further explanation says the question established certainty and removed doubt before the staff became a miracle.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r3.anchor: وقيل: ليقع المعجز بها بعد التثبت وإزالة الشبهة.

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r4.claim: Some say God asked about the staff's uses; after Moses mentioned one use, God indicated further uses, including its role in miracles.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r4.anchor: وقيل: أراد أن يسأله عن منافع العصا، فلما بين بعضه أخبر أن فيه منافع أخر ككونه معجزة له

JISHUMI:v6p4648/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r5.claim: Another explanation takes the question as asking about the staff's uses, like asking about Dhū al-Qarnayn to elicit his story.
JISHUMI:v6p4648/r5.anchor: وقيل إنما سأله عن منافع العصا فلذلك أجاب بالمنافع كقوله: (ويسألونك عن ذي القرنين) أي: عن قصته.

JISHUMI:v6p4651/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r1.claim: A miracle need not be specified in advance; Moses probably already knew his prophethood from God's speech and the signs at the tree, then received the staff and hand as signs for his people.
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r1.anchor: الواجب إظهار معجز من غير تعيين، والأقرب أنه عرف نبوته قبل ذلك لما كلمه، وعرف المعجزات في الشجرة

JISHUMI:v6p4651/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r2.claim: Other explanations say the sign was shown as kindness to Moses or to remove his fear when the staff changed before Pharaoh.
JISHUMI:v6p4651/r2.anchor: وقيل: أظهر ذلك لطفا له، وقيل: لتزول عن قلبه الهيبة عند قلبها بمشهد فرعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r1.claim: Mūsā is parsed as a circumstantial accusative in the sense of pointing, as in 11:72; alternatively, تلك is a relative pronoun with بيمينك as its relative clause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r1.anchor: في انتصاب الحال بمعنى الإشارة : ويجوز أن تكون { تلك } اسما موصولا صلته { بيمينك }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r2.claim: God asks in order to show how He can transform dry wood into a writhing serpent, establish the great difference between the original and transformed things, and draw attention to His overwhelming power; the author compares it to a goldsmith displaying iron transformed into armor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r2.anchor: إنما سأله ليريه عظم ما يخترعه عز وعلا في الخشبة اليابسة من قلبها حية نضناضة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r10.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r10.claim: Some say God asked in order to put Mūsā at ease and reduce his apprehension.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p59/r10.anchor: وقالوا : إنما سأله ليبسط منه ويقلل هيبته

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r1.claim: God's question is confirmatory, not a request for information, so Moses will not doubt after the staff becomes a moving serpent.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p398/r1.anchor: ليس هذا سؤال استفهام , وإنما هو سؤال تقرير لئلا يدخل عليه ارتياب بعد انقلابها حية تسعى

MUQATIL:20:17-18/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:17-18/r1.claim: The object in Moses' right hand was his staff; God asked while intending to transform it into a serpent.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#3/r1.claim: Mā is the subject and tilka its predicate, meaning hādhihi; bi-yamīnika is circumstantial and can mean resting in or held by the right hand, or tilka may be a relative pronoun with bi-yamīnika as its clause.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#3/r1.anchor: ما مبتدأ وتلك خبره هي بمعنى هذه وبيمينك حال عمل فيها معنى الإشارة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#3/r2.claim: God's question draws Moses' attention before the miracle, acclimates him to the staff becoming a snake, or comforts him and removes fear before the conversation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p52#3/r2.anchor: والسؤال للتنبيه لتقع المعجزة بها بعد التثبت أو للتوطين لئلا يهول انقلابها حية

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r1.claim: One view says God’s question to Moses was revelation, since he was told to listen to revelation and a prophet needs a sign by which he knows his own prophethood; the staff and its effects provided one.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r1.anchor: قيل: كان هذا الخطاب من الله تعالى لموسى وحيا لأنه قال: { فاستمع لما يوحى } ولا بد للنبي في نفسه من معجزة

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r2.claim: Alternatively, the sign shown in the tree sufficed for Moses himself, while the hand and staff added confirmation and proof for his people.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ما أراه في الشجرة آية كافية له في نفسه، ثم تكون اليد والعصا زيادة توكيد، وبرهانا يلقى به قومه.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r3.speaker: الزجاج والفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ parse ما as a relative noun linked to بيمينك: what is the thing in your right hand?
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r3.anchor: واختلف في «ما» في قوله: «وما تلك» فقال الزجاج والفراء: هي اسم ناقص وصلت

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also says تلك can mean هذه, and ما ذلك would likewise mean what is that thing.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء أيضا: «تلك» بمعنى هذه ولو قال: ما ذلك لجاز أي ما ذلك الشيء

QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r5.claim: The question elicits Moses’ acknowledgment that it is his staff, establishing the proof through his admission, although God knew its identity eternally.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:17-18/r5.anchor: ومقصود السؤال تقرير الأمر حتى يقول موسى: هي عصاي لتثبت الحجة عليه بعدما اعترف، وإلا فقد علم الله ما هي في الأزل.

QASHANI:20:17-18/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:17-18/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:17-18/r1.claim: The object in Moses' right hand signifies his self in the grasp of intellect, the right hand by which a person receives God's gift and restrains the self.
QASHANI:20:17-18/r1.anchor: العقل يمين يأخذ به الإنسان العطاء من الله ويضبط به نفسه

QASHANI:20:17-18/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:17-18/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:17-18/r5.claim: God asks about the staff to remove the awe caused by the manifestation of majesty and replace it with security.
QASHANI:20:17-18/r5.anchor: وإنما سأله تعالى لإزالة الهيبة الحاصلة له بتجلي العظمة عنه وتبديلها بالأمن

RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r1.claim: The question points separately to the staff with تلك and to Moses' hand with بيمينك; God makes each an overpowering sign, elevating inert matter to a miraculous state.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r1.anchor: قوله : { وما تلك } إشارة إلى العصا ، وقوله : { بيمينك } إشارة إلى اليد

RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r2.claim: As inert matter became living and dense matter subtle, God's daily gaze upon a servant's heart can turn disobedient death into obedience and the light of knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r2.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى ينظر كل يوم ثلاثمائة وستين نظرة إلى قلب العبد ، فأي عجب لو انقلب قلبه

RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r3.claim: As the staff became a serpent that swallowed the magicians' sorcery, divine attention can make the believer's heart swallow the magic of the commanding soul.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r3.anchor: فأي عجب لو صار القلب بمدد النظر الإلهي بحيث يبتلع سحر النفس الأمارة بالسوء

RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r4.claim: As the blessing of Moses' right hand made the staff a sign, God's fingers can turn a believer's heart from the darkness of sin to the light of servitude.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r4.anchor: فإذا حصلت ليمين موسى عليه السلام هذه الكرامة والبركة ، فأي عجب لو انقلب قلب المؤمن

RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r5.claim: God's question does not seek knowledge; it displays the transformation of a lowly object into noble signs and lets Moses first recognize the harmless wooden staff before its transformation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r5.anchor: فالله تعالى لما أراد أن يظهر من العصا تلك الآيات الشريفة كانقلابها حية ، وكضربه البحر حتى انفلق

RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r6.claim: Presenting the staff first as a thing that neither harms nor benefits, then turning it into a great serpent, directs minds to God's power and greatness in making great signs from insignificant things.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r6.anchor: ثم إنه قلبه ثعبانا عظيما ، فيكون بهذا الطريق قد نبه العقول على كمال قدرته ونهاية عظمته

RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r7.claim: The first benefit of the question is to introduce an insignificant object before revealing its noble properties, so listeners identify it before the miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22/r7.anchor: من أراد أن يظهر من الشيء الحقير شيئا شريفا فإنه يأخذه

RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r1.claim: Moses' question also teaches that God asks a bewildered believer in the afterlife about what they knew without error in life, namely monotheism, easing their awe and shyness.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r1.anchor: فيسألونه عن الأمر الذي لم يغلط فيه في الدنيا وهو التوحيد ، فإذا ذكره زالت الدهشة والوحشة عنه

RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r2.claim: God asks about the staff's uses so Moses names some and then learns it has greater uses than he knew, showing that human reason cannot know all the properties of even a present object without divine guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r2.anchor: فسأله عن منافع العصا فذكر بعضها فعرفه الله تعالى أن فيها منافع أعظم مما ذكر

RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r3.claim: The question also establishes firmly for Moses that it is a wooden stick, so he will not fear it when it becomes a serpent.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r3.anchor: فائدة هذا السؤال أن يقرر عنده أنه خشبة حتى إذا قلبها ثعبانا لا يخافها

RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r4.claim: The fact that God speaks to Moses does not prove Moses superior to Muhammad: God also addressed Muhammad in 53:10, but kept that speech secret from others.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r4.anchor: أنه تعالى كما خاطب موسى فقد خاطب محمدا عليه السلام في قوله : { فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r5.claim: The same comparison is answered by noting that Muhammad's community addresses God repeatedly in prayer, and that believers are addressed with greeting and honor in the next life.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r5.anchor: فأمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يخاطبون الله في كل يوم مرات على ما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( المصلي يناجي ربه )

RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r6.claim: Al-Rāzī opens a third question asking for the grammatical parsing of وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى, but the segment ends before his answer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p22#2/r6.anchor: السؤال الثالث : ما إعراب قوله : { وما تلك بيمينك ياموسى * موسى }

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r1.claim: Al-Kashshaf takes the phrase as a circumstantial construction meaning an indicated object, like Hūd 11:72; alternatively, تلك may be a relative pronoun linked to بيمينك.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r1.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ( تلك بيمينك ) كقوله : { وهاذا بعلى شيخا } ( هود : 72 ) في انتصاب الحال بمعنى الإشارة ويجوز

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the question as asking what object is in Moses’ right hand.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج : معناه وما التي بيمينك

RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses the phrase as asking what this thing in Moses’ right hand is.
RAZI-FULL:v22p23/r3.anchor: قال الفراء : معناه ما هذه التي في يمينك

RAZI-FULL:v22p34/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p34/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p34/r1.claim: Moses had received six demanding charges: knowledge of oneness, worship and prayer, the Hereafter, wisdom in God's acts, great signs, and a mission to the most defiant people.
RAZI-FULL:v22p34/r1.anchor: أحدها : معرفة التوحيد : { إننى أنا الله لا إلاه إلا أنا }

QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r9.claim: Moses says the greatest benefit is that God asked what he held; no blessing or use could exceed being addressed by God.
QUSHAYRI:v2p256/r9.anchor: وأعظم مأرب لي فيها أنك قلت : { وما تلك بيمينك ؟ }

STUDYQURAN:20:17/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r1.claim: God's question is rhetorical, drawing Moses' attention to the staff so that he will directly recognize its transformation into a serpent as a miracle.
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r1.anchor: God’s question to Moses is a rhetorical one intended to draw his attention to the staff

STUDYQURAN:20:17/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r2.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī explains that God is making Moses recognize the reality of a piece of wood that can neither harm nor benefit but will become a mighty serpent.
STUDYQURAN:20:17/r2.anchor: Al-Rāzī explains it this way: “It is as if God said, ‘O Moses, do you know the reality of that which is in your hand

TAB-FULL:v16p42/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r1.claim: God asks Moses what is in his right hand, identifying the staff before turning it into a crawling serpent.
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r1.anchor: وما هذه التي في يمينك يا موسى؟

TAB-FULL:v16p42/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r2.claim: The preposition in bi-yamīnika is attached to tilka; Arabs also connect tilka and hādhihi as they do the relative alladhī, illustrated by a line from Yazīd ibn Mufarriġ.
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r2.anchor: العرب تصل تلك وهذه كما تصل الذي، ومنه قول يزيد بن مفرع

TAB-FULL:v16p42/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r3.claim: God draws Moses' attention to the ordinary wooden staff and its uses so he recognizes God's power to transform it and make it a sign for Pharaoh and his people.
TAB-FULL:v16p42/r3.anchor: وإنما قال ذلك عز ذكره له إذا أراد أن يحولها حية تسعى، وهي خشبة، فنبهه عليها

SULAMI:v1p438#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r1.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r1.claim: Faris says Moses was nearly overwhelmed by speech unlike any he had heard; in that ecstatic state he claimed the staff as his own and answered beyond what was asked.
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r1.anchor: قال فارس : سمع موسى كلاما لا يشبه كلام الحق

SULAMI:v1p438#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r2.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r2.claim: When divine attributes overwhelmed Moses, God returned his attention to created things and occupied him with answering so he would not collapse under the sudden address.
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r2.anchor: وقال : لما غلبت عليه الدعات الصفات رده الحق إلى المخلوق

SULAMI:v1p438#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r3.claim: Al-Wasiti says the pleasure of direct address took Moses away from discernment, so he answered both the question asked and one not asked; the staff was a stick to him but a moving serpent in God's knowledge.
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r3.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله : استلذ الخطاب فأخذه عن التمييز

SULAMI:v1p438#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r4.claim: God alone knows the unseen realities of things; by asking Moses what was in his hand, God taught him that he knew only its appearance as a staff, while its reality and transformation were God's domain and display of power.
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى ﴾

SULAMI:v1p438#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r5.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r5.claim: Al-Husayn says God anchored Moses in his description of the staff and had him verify it; changing it into a serpent then exposed Moses' incapacity and provided a sign for the community.
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r5.anchor: وقال الحسين : في قوله : ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك ﴾ قال : أثبته

SULAMI:v1p438#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r6.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r6.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir says God made the question expansive to steady Moses' heart, knowing what would unfold when he witnessed divine majesty.
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r6.anchor: وسمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت أبا بكر بن طاهر يقول

SULAMI:v1p438#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r7.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r7.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Tahir adds that God wanted Moses to speak at length so he would not feel constrained when asking.
SULAMI:v1p438#2/r7.anchor: وقال أيضا : أحب الله تعالى أن يبسط موسى في الكلام

SULAMI:v1p438#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r4.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r4.claim: Junayd says God alone knows hidden realities: Moses named the staff and its known uses, so God disclosed its hidden reality as a serpent beforehand, preventing panic and teaching him to turn back toward God without fear.
SULAMI:v1p438#3/r4.anchor: سمعت منصور بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت جعفر بن نصير يقول سمعت الجنيد

TABATABAI:20:15-17/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:15-17/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:15-17/r11.claim: The question begins the revelation of Moses’s mission; the three preceding verses completed the revelation of prophethood.
TABATABAI:20:15-17/r11.anchor: شروع في وحي الرسالة وقد تم وحي النبوة في الآيات الثلاث الماضية

TABATABAI:20:15-17/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:15-17/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:15-17/r12.claim: The question is for eliciting an answer; Moses is asked to name and describe the staff so he recognizes it as lifeless matter before witnessing its transformation.
TABATABAI:20:15-17/r12.anchor: ليسميها ويذكر أوصافها فيتبين أنها جماد لا حياة له

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r1.claim: The demonstrative apparently refers to the staff or piece of wood; if it referred to an unspecified thing, the wording should be masculine ذلك, which would make the question intelligible as ignorance of what it was.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r1.anchor: ولولا ذلك لكان من حق الكلام أن يقال

TABATABAI:20:18-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r2.claim: Alternatively, تلك points to the known staff but asks for its qualities, not its name; Moses understands this and lists its uses, as one may ask about an obvious thing to elicit description.
TABATABAI:20:18-21/r2.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون الإشارة بتلك إلى العصا لكن لا بداعي الاطلاع على اسمها وحقيقتها حتى يلغو الاستفهام

TABRISI:20:20-23/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:20-23/r1.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:20:20-23/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats tilka as a demonstrative functioning like a relative pronoun, so the question means “what is the thing in your right hand?”
TABRISI:20:20-23/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: تلك اسم مبهم يجري مجرى التي ويوصل كما توصل التي والمعنى وما التي بيمينك

TABRISI:20:20-23/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:20-23/r2.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:20:20-23/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ cites a line using a demonstrative with the sense “the thing that you carry,” supporting the relative-pronoun analysis.
TABRISI:20:20-23/r2.anchor:
وأنشد الفراء:
عدس ما لعباد عليك إمارة

TABRISI:20:20-23/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:20-23/r3.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
TABRISI:20:20-23/r3.claim: A later grammarian makes tilka the subject and puts interrogative mā before its predicate; bi-yamīnika is circumstantial, since demonstratives require specification.
TABRISI:20:20-23/r3.anchor: قال بعض المتأخرين: إن الصحيح الذي لا غبار عليه أن يكون تلك مبتدأ وما خبره قدم عليه لما فيه من معنى الاستفهام

TABRISI:20:20-23/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:20-23/r4.speaker: بعض المتأخرين
TABRISI:20:20-23/r4.claim: This analysis avoids describing an ambiguous demonstrative with a clause, since clauses are indefinite and cannot describe it.
TABRISI:20:20-23/r4.anchor: ولا يجوز وصف المبهم بالجملة لأن الجمل نكرات

FARRA:v2p176/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p176/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p176/r3.claim: تلك refers to Moses’ staff and means “this.”
FARRA:v2p176/r3.anchor: ما تلك بيمينك يا موسى [17] يعني عصاه.

FARRA:v2p176/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p176/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p176/r4.claim: بيمينك complements تلك; demonstratives can take complements like الذي. The anonymous line uses عدس as a mule’s shooing cry and means “the one you carry is free.”
FARRA:v2p176/r4.anchor:
في مذهب صلة لتلك لأن تلك وهذه توصلان كما توصل الذي قال الشاعر .
عدش ما لعباد عليك إمارة ... أمنت وهذا تحملين طليق

THALABI:v6p240/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p240/r13.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v6p240/r13.claim: Moses' staff had two prongs and two points at its base, and Muqātil says it was called nabʿa.
THALABI:v6p240/r13.anchor: وكانت لها شعبتان وفي أسفلها سنان واسمها نبعة في قول مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r1.claim: Abu Ishaq treats tilka as an indefinite demonstrative functioning like the relative pronoun allatī, meaning “that which.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ({تلك} اسم مبهم يجري مجرى التي، ويوصل كما توصل التي ,

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r3.claim: Al-Farra treats bi-yamīnika as a complement of tilka, since demonstratives like tilka and hadhihi can be linked like relative pronouns.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r3.anchor: و {بيمينك} في مذهب صلة لتلك؛ لأن تلك وهذه توصلان كما توصل الذي.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r4.claim: The question draws Moses’ attention to the staff so that he recognizes it before it becomes a miracle and so that he will reflect on it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r4.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (معنى سؤال موسى عما في يده من العصا التنبيه له عليها, ليقع المعجز بها بعد التثبيت فيها والتأمل لها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq explains the question as eliciting Moses’ acknowledgment, so that after the miracle he cannot deny what he identified; he compares asking someone to name water before changing it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p377/r5.anchor: وقد كشف أبو إسحاق عن هذا المعنى فقال: (هذا الكلام لفظه لفظ الاستفهام ومجراه في الكلام مجرى ما يسأل عنه، ويجيب المخاطب بالإقرار به

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r4.claim: God asks Moses what is in his right hand.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:15-18/r4.anchor: { وما تلك } وما التي { بيمينك } في يدك اليمنى؟

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r1.claim: God asks about the staff in Moses’s right hand, although He already knows what it is.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p256/r1.anchor: يسأله عن العصا التي في يده اليمنى وهو أعلم بها

BURHAN:v4p402/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p402/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p402/r2.claim: Interrogative mā means what, takes the sentence’s initial position, and asks about objects or kinds and qualities of non-rational things, or qualities and kinds of rational beings.
BURHAN:v4p402/r2.anchor: الثالث الاستفهامية بمعنى أي شىء ولها صدر الكلام كالشرط ويسأل بها اعيان ما لا يعقل

NAHHAS:v3p35/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p35/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p35/r12.claim: The question is a subject-predicate construction and carries an alerting force.

NAHHAS:v3p35/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p35/r13.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v3p35/r13.claim: Al-Farrāʾ treats تلك as an incomplete demonstrative whose relative clause is بيمينك; Abū Isḥāq leans toward this analysis.
NAHHAS:v3p35/r13.anchor: وزعم الفراء أن تلك ههنا اسم ناقص وصلته بيمينك قال أبو جعفر ورأيت أبا إسحاق يميل إلى هذا القول

NAHHAS:v3p35/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p35/r14.speaker: أبو العباس
NAHHAS:v3p35/r14.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās rejects that analysis: demonstrative words cannot be used as relative pronouns.
NAHHAS:v3p35/r14.anchor: سمعت علي بن سليمان يقول سمعت أبا العباس ينكر هذا القول ويقول لا يجوز أن توصل الأسماء المبهمة

ITQAN:v2p574/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p574/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p574/r2.claim: Moses gives more than the requested identification of the staff, adding its uses because he delights in being addressed by God.
ITQAN:v2p574/r2.anchor: وقول موسى ﴿ هي عصاي أتوكأ عليها وأهش بها على غنمي ﴾ في جواب ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى ﴾ زاد في الجواب استلذاذا بخطاب الله تعالى

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r1.claim: The image makes darkness a routed enemy fleeing the sword it drew, giving the scene human fear and motion.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r1.anchor: فتوصل إلى ذلك بأن جعل الظلام كالعدو المنهزم الذي سل السيف في قفاه فهو يهرب مخافة أن يضرب به

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r2.claim: A similar poem depicts dawn as an ambusher and night as wary; Jurjānī says al-Khālidī lifted its first line and recast dawn as drawing swords while night flees.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r2.anchor: وقد أخذ الخالدى بيته الأول أخذا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r3.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz makes the rose a conscious victor that laughs at the narcissus as its season ends; this intensifies the conventional image of a blooming rose and reverses Ibn al-Rūmī’s account of their roles.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r3.anchor: وجعل الورد كأنه يعقل ويميز فهو يشمت بالنرجس لانقضاء مدته وإبار دولته وبدو أمارات الفناء فيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r4.claim: Ibn al-Muʿtazz’s gray hair laughs at a man’s ill-fitting attempt to act young, unlike Daʿbal’s bare reversal; the added motive makes the simile less explicit and more vivid.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p255/r4.anchor: جعل المشيب يضحك ضحك المتعجب من تعاطى الرجل ما لا يليق به وتكلفه الشيء ليس هو من أهله

TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r4.claim: God asks about the staff in Moses' hand to draw his attention to it and let the ensuing miracle occur after he has examined it.
TABRISI:20:17-36#2/r4.anchor: سأله عما في يده من العصا تنبيها له عليها ليقع المعجز بها

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r14.claim: God repeated questions about the staff in several verses because He knew it would become the setting for a great miracle.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r14.anchor: كرر عليه السؤال في غير آية من عصاه لما كان المعلوم له سبحانه فيها من إظهاره فيها عظيم المعجزة

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r15.claim: Another explanation is that Moses' sudden awe at hearing God's address was eased by returning him to the staff and its signs.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r15.anchor: ويقال إنما قال ذلك لأنه صحبته هيبة المقام عند فجأة سماع الخطاب ، فليسكن بعض ما به من بواده الإجلال

QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r16.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r16.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r16.claim: If Moses had remained under the force of awe, he might not have understood or been able to bear the encounter.
QUSHAYRI:v2p255/r16.anchor: لعله كان لا يعي ولا يطيق ذلك

BURHAN:v4p42/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p42/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p42/r6.claim: God’s question to Moses about what is in his right hand matches the question and adds information.
BURHAN:v4p42/r6.anchor: ونظيره ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى ﴾ 3 فيكون طابق وزاد

BURHAN:v2p342/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p342/r10.claim: The thirteenth use is reassurance or familiarity, exemplified by God's question to Moses about his staff.
BURHAN:v2p342/r10.anchor: الثالث عشر الإيناس نحو ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى ﴾

BURHAN:v2p342/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r11.speaker: ابن فارس
BURHAN:v2p342/r11.claim: Ibn Fāris calls the question imparting understanding: God reveals what Moses did not know about the staff.
BURHAN:v2p342/r11.anchor: وقال ابن فارس المراد به ( 3 ) الإفهام فان الله تعالى قد علم ان لها امرا قد خفي على موسى

BURHAN:v2p342/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p342/r12.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v2p342/r12.claim: Another view says the question identifies Moses' object so he will not be startled when it becomes a serpent.
BURHAN:v2p342/r12.anchor: وقيل هو للتقرير فيعرف مافي يده حتى لاينفر إذا انقلبت حية

BURHAN:v4p44/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p44/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p44/r7.claim: Moses expanded his answer about the object in his hand because he sensed that a great event involving the staff was coming and wanted to describe its ordinary uses first.
BURHAN:v4p44/r7.anchor: ومثال الزيادة في الجواب قوله تعالى

ITQAN:v3p215/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p215/r14.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p215/r14.claim: Interrogation can reassure or put the addressee at ease, as in Moses being asked what he holds in his right hand.
ITQAN:v3p215/r14.anchor: التاسع والعشرون الإيناس نحو ﴿ وما تلك بيمينك يا موسى ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p641#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p641#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p641#2/r2.claim: Yamīn can mean the right hand itself, as in Moses’s question.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p641#2/r2.anchor: أحدها : العضو المعروف الذي تماثله الشمال . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة طه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p170/r9.claim: Questions may function as confirmation rather than requests for unknown information, as in questions to Jesus, Moses, and communities addressed by messengers.

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r14.claim: One explanation treats bi-yamīnika as completing the demonstrative phrase, as with relative pronouns.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r14.anchor: قيل: بيمينك صلة (تلك)، كما أوصل التي والذي

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r15.claim: Another explanation says Moses was so bewildered by the wonders that he could not distinguish right from left, so the question specified which hand.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r15.anchor: وقيل: لما كلمه ورأى تلك العجائب تحير حتى كان لا يعرف اليمين من الشمال

JISHUMI:v6p4646/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r16.claim: The passage introduces the miracles God gave Moses and the command that he convey the message.
JISHUMI:v6p4646/r16.anchor: ثم بين تعالى ما أعطى موسى من المعجزات وما أمره بالتبليغ
